content:
Yuki Sato: heads up on B200 bring-up: first two early-access nodes in bench-lab are not behaving like our H100/L40S assumptions. seeing driver/CUDA mismatches + unusually high kernel fallback %.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1, infra side: these are "early" images, not on our standard runtime-1.22 base. one node is on 550.xx, another on 555.xx. i can normalize but want to make sure runtime fails safely if this happens in customer private too.

Irene Choi: can you paste the exact error? want to know if it’s hard fail or silent perf regression.

Yuki Sato: from `redwood-runtime` startup logs (B200-01):
```text
[hw_detect] gpu=NVidia B200-SXM
[hw_detect] driver=550.54.14 cuda_runtime=12.4
[runtime] loading profile pack version=1.0.0
[profiles] selected profile_id=b200-preview-default
[kernels] attention_v3 enabled
[kernels] WARN falling back to attention_v2 reason="sm90a kernel requires driver>=555" count=712
```
then a bit later, during model load:
```text
CUDA error: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
  at cudart::cudaGetDeviceProperties
```

Noah Patel: that’s the worst combo (partial boot, then hard error at load). we can’t let this “kinda starts” state happen. should refuse to start *before* accepting traffic if compatibility isn’t satisfied.

Hiro Tanaka: the fallback warning is expected-ish if driver is too old for the sm90a path, but the cudart mismatch suggests container cuda runtime > host driver in that image.

Omar El-Sayed: also seeing weird allocator behavior on B200-02 when it doesn’t crash: fragmentation estimate spikes and KV cache compaction time goes way up (probably because we’re not using the kernels we think we are).

Quentin Harris: this is exactly why we talked about a hard compatibility gate. B200 has too much surface area (driver + cuda + firmware?) to be “best effort”. we should make it: (a) require explicit `profile_version` pin AND (b) enforce driver/CUDA minimums in runtime on startup.

Neha Kapoor: infra POV: we *will* have variance for a bit as we ramp B200. but we can commit to a baseline once the fleet plan is locked. until then, runtime gate is the right safety belt.

Vanessa Ortiz: agreed. we can’t have Hosted silently running a "B200" pool that’s actually behaving like something else. can we make the gate message super explicit and actionable for on-call? like: detected driver X, required >= Y for profile pack Z.

Rafael Mendes: from rollout safety angle: gate should be a hard block + clear alert, not a slow degradation. otherwise we’ll chase p99 regressions that are just compatibility drift.

Yuki Sato: +1. proposal: for any `sku=B200*` we do NOT auto-select “best known” unless `profile_version` is pinned (or control plane sets it). if missing, we exit with non-zero and log a single-line reason.

Noah Patel: careful: Hosted control plane *will* set it, Private might not. but forcing explicit pin for Private seems fine (it’s preview hardware). we can have installer warn too.

Quentin Harris: yep. gate rules (first cut):
- sku==B200 => require `profile_version` explicitly set (no default)
- enforce `driver_version >= min_driver` and `cuda >= min_cuda` as declared in the profile pack manifest
- if not satisfied => `FATAL profiles_incompatible` and refuse to serve
- emit metric `runtime_profile_compatibility=0/1` + include reason label (bounded)

Hiro Tanaka: we should also gate on kernel availability: if profile expects `attention_v3` but we’d fall back >N% in warmup, we should treat as incompatible. otherwise people run “B200 profile” but never hit the intended kernels.

Omar El-Sayed: +1, but make it deterministic. we can do a static check on driver/cuda + arch; avoid warmup heuristics if possible.

Irene Choi: what’s the immediate action? can we track in Linear + get a PR in before next bench run?

Yuki Sato: i’ll open/update ENG-4928 (B200 bring-up checklist) with: “hard compatibility gate required” + expected log strings. also linking this thread.

Vanessa Ortiz: and i’ll file infra task to standardize these nodes (driver + base image). but runtime still needs to protect us.

Redwood CI Bot: Yuki Sato created ENG-4928: "B200 bring-up checklist (early fleet): compatibility gate, benchmark matrix subset, and rollback plan" <https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4928>

Noah Patel: implementation suggestion: add a `compatibility` section to the profile pack schema (min_driver, min_cuda, allowed_instance_types optional) and validate at startup. make it part of the config loader so it runs before model init.

Quentin Harris: I can take schema updates + validation rules, Yuki can wire into selection logic. seems aligned with PR-24927 direction.

Neha Kapoor: please include in the failure output which team owns the fix (infra vs runtime) so on-call knows who to page.

Rafael Mendes: and make sure there’s a kill switch for Hosted: if a region starts failing gate, we can route traffic away / drain pool cleanly.

Hiro Tanaka: can we also log the detected `sm` + GPU firmware revision? we’ve seen B200 nodes report slightly different revs.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 but keep cardinality sane. maybe add to startup log + debug endpoint, not as metric labels.

Yuki Sato: ok, summary:
- hard compatibility gate for B200 (no silent fallback)
- require explicit profile_version pin for B200 preview
- enforce min driver/cuda from profile pack
- improve error msg + single clear metric + log, no high-cardinality labels

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: i’ll update bench-lab images today so we can keep running smoke tests, but let’s still land the gate before we widen the pool.

Quentin Harris: i’ll draft the schema addition + send for quick review in #eng-runtime.

Noah Patel: sounds good. please post the exact fatal string in the doc so SRE can grep it.

Yuki Sato: will do. will also add a note that B200 is “preview: explicit pin required” so Product doesn’t assume Dedicated customers can just upgrade and get it.
